lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: Say What You Think and Why
lesson.summary: Speak loudly and clearly, give one reason with because, and listen politely.
lesson.unit: Topic 10: Say what you think and why
learning_objectives: Share an opinion in a full sentence

standards.text: Articulate and justify answers, arguments and opinions; listen and respond to others; speak audibly in full sentences

success_criteria: I can say what I think
I can add a reason with because
I can listen and reply kindly
lesson.real_life: Favourite Eid food, a favourite cricket player, show-and-tell in the UK, and class recitation in Pakistan.

warm_up.prompt: An opinion is what someone thinks.
warm_up.explanation: An opinion is what you think.

warm_up.prompt: How should you speak to the class?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we say what we think, and why?
blocks.say: Today we share what we think. We also say why.

blocks.alt: Seven plates of colourful sugary sweets in different shapes arranged on a green table
blocks.caption: Which sweet do you like best? Your answer is your opinion.
blocks.credit: Photo by Analia Baggiano on Unsplash
blocks.say: Look at these sweets. Which would you pick? Everyone may choose differently.

blocks.markdown: An **opinion** is what you think or feel.
blocks.say: An opinion is what someone thinks or feels. It is not a fact.

scenes.caption: A fact.
scenes.say: A mango is a fruit. That is a fact. It is true for everyone.

scenes.caption: An opinion.
scenes.say: Mangoes are the best fruit. That is an opinion. Others may disagree.

scenes.caption: Your opinion.
scenes.say: Your opinion is yours. You can say it and give a reason.

blocks.markdown: A **reason** says why. Use **because** to join them.
blocks.say: A reason says why we think it. We join an opinion and a reason with because.

scenes.caption: Because.
scenes.say: I like gulab jamun because they are sweet and soft.

scenes.caption: A good reason.
scenes.say: The reason must fit the opinion. A sweet taste fits liking sweets.

scenes.caption: One reason.
scenes.say: One clear reason is enough. We do not need a long list.

question.prompt: The word because joins an opinion to its reason.

blocks.title: Aisha and the Eid dessert
blocks.transcript: Our topic today is the best Eid dessert. I think sheer khurma is the best. That is my opinion. I think so because it is creamy and sweet. She speaks loudly and clearly. She looks at the class. Omar says, I see it differently. I like jalebi. He says, I like it because it is crunchy. Aisha listens carefully. She does not interrupt. They disagree, but they stay kind. Both choices are good!
blocks.caption: Aisha tells which Eid dessert is best and why, then listens to Omar.

points: An opinion is what you think
blocks.say: Let us remember. An opinion is what you think. A reason says why. Join them with because.

terms.meaning: What you think or feel about something.
Something that is true.
Why you think or feel something.
A word that gives the reason.

mini_quiz.explanation: An opinion is what you think or feel.

blocks.say: A good talker uses a clear voice. Not too loud and not too quiet.

scenes.caption: Loud enough.
scenes.say: Speak loud enough for the back row to hear. Do not shout.

scenes.caption: A good pace.
scenes.say: Go slowly. Pause between ideas so people can think.

scenes.caption: Clear words.
scenes.say: Say each word clearly. Finish every sentence.

blocks.alt: Blue chairs arranged in a circle seen from above
blocks.caption: Chairs in a circle for a group talk. Everyone can see everyone.
blocks.credit: Photo by ObjectType RAW on Unsplash
blocks.say: Look at your audience. Eye contact shows you care about them.
Stand tall and stay calm. Smile if you can.

blocks.title: Helps or not?
blocks.goal: Move each tip. Good tips go in Helps. Bad tips go in Not helping.
blocks.say: Now sort these tips. Do they help us speak well, or not?

blocks.title: Practise a talk
instructions: Say: I think my favourite sweet is...
Practise a clear voice and eye contact.

question.prompt: Put the talk steps in order.
question.explanation: We think, then speak, then thank.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Speak clearly, look at your audience, and finish each sentence.

terms.meaning: In a way that is easy to understand.
Looking at someone's eyes when you speak.
How fast you speak.
A short stop.
Not worried or rushed.

mini_quiz.prompt: Eye contact shows we care about our audience.
What should we say in a full sentence?
mini_quiz.explanation: A full sentence says a whole idea.

blocks.markdown: **Agree** means you think the same. **Disagree** means you think differently.
blocks.say: In this game we move to a side. Do we agree, or do we disagree?

scenes.caption: Agree.
scenes.say: Layla says rain is lovely. Aisha agrees because it feeds the plants.

scenes.caption: Disagree.
scenes.say: Omar disagrees. He likes sunny days because he can play outside.

scenes.caption: Polite.
scenes.say: Both give a reason. Both are polite. They can still be friends.

blocks.markdown: Play the game, then answer a question.
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the pictures light up, then copy them.

blocks.title: Talk time
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Watch the order closely. Then copy it.

points: We listen first and are polite
blocks.say: Let us remember. We can agree or disagree politely. We always listen first.

terms.meaning: To think the same as someone.
To think differently from someone.
Kind and respectful.
To talk when someone else is talking.
Your time to speak.

mini_quiz.explanation: It is polite and gives a reason.

blocks.say: Plan a short talk. Choose a topic you care about.

blocks.markdown: A good topic: a favourite Eid food.
blocks.say: In Pakistan, many children pick a favourite Eid dessert like sheer khurma.

blocks.markdown: Another topic: a favourite cricket player.
blocks.say: Others like cricket. Babar Azam and Joe Root both have fans.
In the UK, a class might talk about a favourite show-and-tell treasure.

scenes.caption: Opinion.
scenes.say: I think sheer khurma is the best Eid dessert. That is my opinion.

scenes.caption: Reason.
scenes.say: I think so because it is creamy and sweet. That is my reason.

scenes.caption: Thanks.
scenes.say: Thank you for listening. Now I would like to hear your idea.

question.prompt: Which is the best reason for: Eid is the best day?
question.explanation: Sharing and visiting family fits liking Eid.

options.text: We share food and visit family

blocks.say: When someone finishes, reply kindly. You can agree or disagree.

scenes.caption: Listen.
scenes.say: Aisha finishes her talk. Omar listens with his ears and eyes.

scenes.caption: Reply.
scenes.say: Omar replies, I see it differently, because I like jalebi.

scenes.caption: Thanks.
scenes.say: They thank each other. Both choices are fine.

blocks.title: Mini debate
instructions: Each person says an opinion and a reason.
Listen to each other, then reply kindly.

question.prompt: We can change our mind if we hear a good reason.

points: Say an opinion and give a reason
Reply kindly, and change your mind if you want
blocks.say: Let us remember. Say what you think, give a reason, listen and reply kindly.
